key_insight: The paper argues that VLA models need more than visual-language understanding: they also need an explicit motion prior. By learning action priors, the model can better transfer manipulation skills across different robot bodies instead of relearning motion from scratch.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of training Vision-Language-Action policies when the action module must simultaneously learn temporal motion patterns, cross-modal alignment, and robot-specific control dynamics. This is especially challenging for cross-embodiment manipulation, where the same task must work across robots with different physical structures.
method: Attach or learn an action-prior module that captures reusable motion patterns before/alongside policy learning.
Use the prior to guide the action module so it does not start from a blank slate for physical control.
Train for cross-embodiment generalization so manipulation policies transfer across different robot embodiments.
impact: For practitioners, this can reduce data inefficiency and improve robustness when deploying manipulation policies on new robots. It is especially useful for building scalable VLA systems that generalize beyond a single robot platform.
